text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- The office for free competition says national broadcasting company YLE should give up its right to collect public fees from commercial TV channels because fees distort competition among electronic media.
- Poll shows President Martti Ahtisaari most popular among voters as next president followed by UN Bosnia human rights observer Elisabeth Rehn and Speaker of parliament Riitta Uosukainen.
- Finnish customs confiscated 18.5 kg of hashis, the largest quantity this year, from an Israeli Palestinian.
- Visiting Czech Republic defence minister says his country's historical experience provides ample reason to join NATO.
- Female private sector lawyers in Finland earn nearly 10 percent less than male colleagues, study shows.
- Lower profitability in forest industry and other sectors seen reducing investment by 16 percent next year, Finnish industry and employer confederation says.
- Valmet's Valmet Automotive seeking western partner for car assembly plant which it plans to build in Russia near Finnish border.
- According to First Call, eight Wall Street investment banks have adjusted upward their profit forecasts for Nokia after Nokia's nine-month interim report.
- Stockholm bourse wants to end listed companies' practice of holding closed conferences with analysts, from which media are excluded.
- Social Democrat parliamentary group supports government proposal to reform regional administration by trimming the number of mainland provinces to five from 11.

- Having just introduced new national trunk telephone numbers, Finland not keen on European Commission proposal for common trunk telephone numbers throughout the continent, Finnish telecoms authorities say.
